audit.why: 45.68% over 637 games — the second-worst in this slice — and the chart is appropriately grim: Camille gets levels 2-3 and the item stages only on paper, with the prose stating plainly that Wukong reclaims the lane at first item and out-skirmishes her at full build. The organising idea, that her whole game is the level-6 window, matches the numbers.

Level 6 as the one clean window and first item as Wukong's reclaim are both right. Cyclone is 130s at rank 1 falling to 90s — a long enough cooldown that a spent Cyclone genuinely opens the dive the text is asking for, which is worth saying.

audit.whatIsWrong: Warrior Trickster is referred to nine times as 'his W', 'his W decoy' and 'W stealth-reposition' and never named. Stone Skin is never named — his armour stacking is described as if it were an item choice ('once Wukong has armor', 'his armor stacking'). Camille's R appears without its article.
audit.why: Riot's kit: Stone Skin (P) is the passive that stacks armour and health from nearby enemies — it is not something he buys, which changes how the 'stack armour to beat her' framing should read. Warrior Trickster (W) is the decoy plus dash, and it is 22s at rank 1, dropping only to 18s at rank 5. That number is the entire matchup: the text tells you five separate times to bait the clone before committing, and 22s is a genuinely long punish window against Hookshot's 16s — Camille's engage comes back before his decoy does. Nimbus Strike is 10s and Crushing Blow is 8s.
audit.corrected: Stone Skin and Warrior Trickster named; Warrior Trickster's 22s stated so 'bait the clone' becomes a countable window; Nimbus Strike's 10s and Cyclone's 130s written in.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Bait or wait out his W decoy before you spend E', 'only commit when you've confirmed the real body', 'ideally when his Nimbus Strike dash is down' — the three central instructions all name cooldowns and none gives a duration.
audit.why: Warrior Trickster at 22s against Hookshot at 16s is the single most encouraging fact available in a 45.68% matchup: if you make him spend the decoy, your engage is back six seconds before his escape is. Nimbus Strike at 10s is not a window worth waiting for by comparison, so the text currently points the reader at the wrong one of the two.
audit.corrected: 22s vs 16s written into wants.you[0] and mid; Nimbus Strike's 10s given so the reader can see which cooldown actually matters.

audit.whatIsWrong: early says your passive shield 'recharges on a timer so he can bait it'.
audit.why: Adaptive Defenses is granted when Camille's own basic attack lands on a champion — it does not sit charged waiting to be baited, and it adapts to the damage type of the attacker. Against Wukong that means it is armour-type mitigation you only get by attacking him first, which inverts the advice: you cannot hold it in reserve during a poke exchange you are not participating in.
audit.corrected: Restated as a shield you have to earn by landing an attack.

edits.before: Wukong owns Levels 1-2 here — his Q (Crushing Blow) resets his auto and shreds your armor while you only have Precision Protocol, so don't step up to trade or bodyblock his autos; just last-hit and eat the chip. Your passive shield helps you survive a poke, but it recharges on a timer so he can bait it. By 3 you have a point in E and your Q recast for the true-damage second hit, which lets you contest short trades, but his W decoy is the whole problem: blow E-stun or your empowered Q onto the clone and you've spent your engage for nothing. Wait until the real body commits, then trade and heal off W's outer edge.
edits.after: Wukong owns Levels 1-2 here — Crushing Blow resets his auto and shreds your armour while you only have Precision Protocol, so don't step up to trade or bodyblock his autos; just last-hit and eat the chip. Adaptive Defenses only appears once your own attack lands on him, so it is not a shield you can hold in reserve through his poke. By 3 you have a point in E and the Q recast for the true-damage second hit, but Warrior Trickster is the whole problem: spend your engage on the clone and it is gone for 16s. Wait for the real body, then trade and heal off W's outer edge.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay a coin-flip because his W keeps baiting your commit, but Level 6 is your window — Hextech Ultimatum traps the real Wukong in an arena he can't walk out of, so his W stealth-reposition and Nimbus Strike can't peel him to safety like they do in open lane. Force the all-in: E-stun in, R to lock him, then land the Q recast for true damage and heal the exchange with W. Watch his R (Cyclone) — if he lands the spin knock-up mid-combo he'll interrupt your follow-up, so bait it or save your dash to reposition out of it.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay a coin-flip because Warrior Trickster keeps baiting your commit — but it is 22s against your 16s Hookshot, so making him spend it is a real window. Level 6 is yours: The Hextech Ultimatum traps the real Wukong in an arena where a spent decoy and a 10s Nimbus Strike can't peel him to safety like they do in open lane. Force the all-in: E in, R to lock him, land the Q recast for true damage and heal the exchange with W. Watch Cyclone — a 130s spin knock-up landing mid-combo interrupts your follow-up, so bait it or save your dash for it.

notes: The whole matchup is built on 'bait the clone' and never once says Warrior Trickster is a 22s cooldown against Camille's 16s Hookshot — which is the one genuinely favourable piece of arithmetic in a 45.68% lane. Stone Skin was also never named, leaving his armour described as though it were purely an item decision. Corrected the description of Camille's own passive as well: it was written as a shield that 'recharges on a timer so he can bait it', but Riot grants it when her attack lands on a champion, so it cannot be held back through a poke exchange she is not part of.
